Subject: MAP Weekly: Data governance & deployment-mode decision log

Hi Alyssa / team —

Quick recap from today's MAP checkpoint and the open decisions we said we'd close this week around data handling and deployment mode. Attaching the updated MAP workbook (FinTechOps-MAP-v2.xlsx) with the tracker: column "Decision" (pending/approved), "Owner", and "Target close".

Summary of open items:
- Decision A: Primary deployment mode for PII workloads (VPC-hosted Redwood Dedicated vs on-prem installation).
- Decision B: Retention and purge policy for transaction logs and user-level embeddings.
- Decision C: KMS/HSM key management and encryption-at-rest responsibilities.

Action items and owners (short):
1) Customer detailed constraints doc (Alyssa) — due EOD Thu — will confirm whether on-prem is required for production PII.
2) Redwood technical feasibility + ops runbook (Priyom) — draft by Fri COB.
3) SOC2 evidence and compliance intake (Marissa) — provide initial packet and mapping to their questionnaire by Thu morning.
4) Contract/Procurement checklist (Lauren) — coordinate with Procurement after decision on deployment mode.

Questions we flagged that need clear answers this week:
- If FinTech Ops requires on-prem, do they need air-gapped install or is a VPC with customer-controlled routing sufficient? (impacts timeline + license model)
- Retention: recommended default is 90 days for conversational logs; do you need stricter retention or per-tenant retention windows?

Alyssa — can you confirm the short answers in reply and attach any internal compliance FAQ you want us to review?

Thanks,
Lauren

lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@fintech-ops.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintech-ops.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP Weekly: Data governance & deployment-mode decision log

Thanks for the clear notes, Lauren —

Short answers from my side this morning:
- Deployment mode: For our regulated payments product, we need customer-controlled infrastructure. Preferred approach is on-prem installation for any workload that touches unmasked PII (payment instrument data, full account numbers). For lower-sensitivity inference (anonymized scoring), VPC with customer-managed routing is acceptable.
- Retention: For PII, retention must be no more than 30 days unless there's an explicit audit log exception. For anonymized logs, 180 days is acceptable.
- KMS: We require customer-managed keys (HSM-backed) for production PII workloads; if Redwood can integrate with our on-prem HSM or support a bring-your-own-key flow, that's a path forward.

I don't have the full compliance FAQ in one place yet — looping in Procurement who will push the formal questionnaire and the internal security contact.

Alyssa Chen
Head of Compliance, FinTech Ops
alyssa.chen@fintech-ops.com
[Procurement included above for intake]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@fintech-ops.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP Weekly: Data governance & deployment-mode decision log

Thanks Alyssa — great clarity. Technical notes and a proposed split-mode plan:

On-prem vs VPC approach (high level):
- On-prem (for PII): Redwood can provide an on-prem appliance bundle (containerized inference + control plane shim) that runs behind customer network. Requirements: NW routing to allow limited control-plane telemetry (optional), air-gap options available but add ~6 weeks to install & validation.
- VPC (for anonymized scoring): Redwood Dedicated in customer VPC with customer-managed route table and KMS integration. Quicker to production (~2-3 weeks for setup).

Retention & PII handling:
- We can support per-tenant retention windows enforced at the gateway for both modes. Default retention config: 30d for PII workloads, 180d for anonymized logs — will be configurable.
- We will implement token-level redaction and offer a pre-processing hook to strip or hash sensitive fields before upstreaming to the model. Work to be owned by Priyom (engineering runbook).

KMS/HSM:
- Integration options: (1) Redwood integrates with customer KMS via standard APIs (recommended for VPC), (2) For on-prem we can support direct HSM connectors or provide an agent that proxies calls to customer HSM. Both require an HSM handshake and key rotation policy agreement.

Risks and timeline impact:
- Air-gapped on-prem installs: +6 weeks for installation and security validation; requires onsite ops access.
- Per-tenant retention enforcement: +1 week dev to enable policy flags; testing +2 weeks.

Proposed owners and near-term commits:
- Priyom: on-prem runbook + initial deployment template (due 2026-12-03).
- Marissa: compliance packet (SOC2-evidence-request.pdf) to Alyssa + mapping to their questionnaire (due 2026-12-02).
- Lauren: coordinate procurement path & prepare draft SOW for on-prem license (target 2026-12-04).

I'll attach a short ops checklist and SOC2 pointer separately. 

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
[Attachment: SOC2-evidence-request.pdf (doc stub)]
